newsitem.title: REUNION: New demonstrations on French Indian Ocean island.
newsitem.headline: New demonstrations on French Indian Ocean island.

text.p: New clashes broke out on Friday on the French Indian Ocean island of Reunion, where dozens of cars were torched and shops looted on Thursday, police said.
Police fired tear gas to disperse several thousand demonstrators, mostly civil servants and students, who stormed the local elected assembly building after staging a protest rally on Friday.
Some 28 people were arrested on Thursday during violence by groups of youths in the dilapidated Chaudron neighbourhood of the usually quiet tropical city, police said.
The unrest began with demonstrations timed to coincide with protests by civil servants in France, angered at a government decision not to compensate for a freeze on civil service salaries last year.

Resentment is especially intense in Reunion because of plans to start phasing out the extra 30-odd percent in salaries is paid to civil servants stationed in France's overseas possessions, including those locally recruited.
Reunion, with a mixed population of 600,000 Creoles, Indians, Chinese and Europeans is broadly divided into two societies living side-by-side.
One is made up of people on the government payroll, ranging from top officials to sanitation workers, who have a European standard of living due to salaries higher than those in France itself.
The other lives in poverty because of massive unemployment in the failing sugar cane industry.
